about: Allow list for tools/shadow-diff.py on edf_native_shadow_render captures. Every rule is an expected exclusion (the shadow render's own design) or a capture limitation of lists recorded before the tap kept only the slots a pipeline's shaders read (reflected=false). Real renderer discrepancies are deliberately NOT here: model vertex constants, the pre-sampler-restore post difference and the image pixels stay reported. Rules marked reflected=false stop matching once captures are reflected, so a stale-slot excuse cannot hide a real missing input there.

draws.reason: tone hold: the guest post's PS_Downsample_Tone draw is held so the GPU tone history blends once per frame
draws.evidence: kNativeShadowExclusions 'tone'; one extra native.post draw per frame, 1x1 target, the only 400106f0 draw; shadow.json held.tone=1 on all 16 frames

draws.reason: the post's resolve copies (conv shaders) set no constants: their constant slots hold the previous draw's, which after the held tone draw is the tone draw's on the native side and the previous copy's on the guest side
draws.evidence: native#626 ps0 = the tone draw's ps0 hash, guest#695 ps0 = the 2x2 copy's; same source texture, same 1x1 target

draws.reason: post passes: slots 1-3 hold what the scene passes left bound (native: the 2048x2048 shadow cascades; guest: its last material's) and the quad vertex shader's constant slot the previous shader's; slot 0 (the pass input), the tone and bloom inputs, the pixel constants and the targets all match
draws.evidence: every native.post pair matches on texture.1.0, ps constants and targets; frames 4060-4900 post output matches to +-1 except geometry edges

draws.reason: slot 4 on static world materials: the guest leaves the 256x256 texture every guest draw had in slot 4 bound; the native material binds only its declared textures
draws.evidence: 515 of 2312 static world instances, 5 materials; everything else on them matches. Open: whether these pixel shaders read slot 4 (a reflected capture reports texture.1.4.missing if they do)

draws.reason: the native models pass draws its opaque items in its own order; the guest draws them in callback order. An opaque depth-tested draw's order matters only at exact depth ties. A blending draw has the field 'blended' and is not excused
draws.evidence: log 'Native full frame models: opaque=180 transparent=0 blended=0'; 187-191 reorders per frame, all within native.models
